newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Cosco Investment to sell Jurong workshop.
newsitem.headline: Cosco Investment to sell Jurong workshop.

text.p: Cosco Investment (Singapore) Ltd is talking to buyers about selling its workshop in Jurong and its marine unit will seek the approval of the Jurong Town Corporation (JTC) shortly, company president Lu Hong Fei said on Monday.

Lu said the company would seek JTC approval for the sale of a three-storey ship repair workshop-cum-office in Jurong and Cosco Marine would discussing the issue with the council on Tuesday or Wednesday.
"We are looking to sell the workshop. Now we are talking with some buyers," Lu told Reuters.

"If we continue to hold on to the building, the loss we calculated (from depreciation and interest payments to the banks) is expected around Singapore $700,000 per year," Lu said. "If we sell the workshop, we could expect a profit of S$100,000 to S$200,000 per year."
He said the move to sell the workshop was prompted by the slowdown in ship-repair business in Singapore and the very small annual repair volumes.
Lu said Singapore's high labour costs, five times higher than in China, reinforced the decision.
In February 1994, Cosco acquired 60 percent of the issued and paid-up capital of Cosco Marine, a marine engineering and ship repair company.
While Cosco Investment's shiprepair business made a profit of S$100,000 in 1995, its contribution was negligible in the first six months of this year, Lu said.

Analysts say the long-awaited recovery of the business in Singapore remained elusive and new docks opened by Keppel and Jurong added to the industry's woes -- too many yards and not that many ships to repair.
Combined shiprepair profits of the three yards -- Keppel Shipyard, Sembawang Shipyard and Jurong Shipyard -- have slumped to about Singapore $27 million (US$19 million) in the first half of the year.
Analysts say the second half was not expected to be much better.
In the heyday of 1991 and 1992, shiprepair profits for the three yards amounted to S$245 million.
